gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many 4K ProRes 422 HQ streams each candidate's *measured* path actually carries: 16 for the QNAP TBS-h574TX over Thunderbolt 4 on a Mac (1,850 MB/s), 9 for the UGREEN DXP480T Plus over 10GbE (1,059 MB/s), but only 3 for the UGREEN DXP6800 Pro's six-HDD RAID 5 over 10GbE (421 MB/s), against the 11-stream link ceiling rivals quote.
standout_why: esp32.co.uk (cited) divides the raw 10GbE line rate by ProRes rates (11 / 7 / 5 streams) but never applies measured product throughput; wundertech.net (cited) gives UGREEN's own 600–700 MB/s RAID 5 claim for the DXP4800 Plus and a drive-count rule, with no codec rates or stream counts. Neither shows that a six-HDD RAID 5 on the DXP6800 Pro measured 421 MB/s over 10GbE (ComputerBase), a third of the link, nor derives Thunderbolt-on-Mac vs Thunderbolt-on-Windows stream counts for the TBS-h574TX (16 vs 9), nor prices per measured MB/s.
decides: Confirms the DXP6800 Pro as the HDD-pool pick for a single editor (3–4 ProRes 422 HQ UHD streams from six IronWolf Pro drives, 6 from its NVMe volume), but shows that anyone cutting multicam or 4444 needs flash: the DXP480T Plus delivers 9 streams per 10GbE link for $0.85 per measured MB/s, and the TBS-h574TX 16 streams over Thunderbolt 4 on a Mac for $0.78 per MB/s, falling to 9 on Windows where TB4 networking measured barely above 10GbE. The 25 GB Thunderbolt copy on the DXP6800 Pro ran at 424 MB/s read, so Thunderbolt does not rescue an HDD pool.

findings.label: ProRes 422 HQ target data rate, 1920×1080 at 29.97 fps (Apple)
findings.note: Apple's table also lists 422 Proxy 45, LT 102, 422 147, 4444 330, 4444 XQ 500 Mb/s at 1080p29.97. Page dated March 3, 2025.

findings.label: ProRes 422 HQ per-stream rate, 3840×2160 at 29.97 fps (derived)
findings.note: UHD has 4× the pixels of 1080p and ProRes scales with pixel count: 220 Mb/s × 4 = 880 Mb/s ÷ 8 = 110 MB/s. Matches the ~880 Mb/s (~110 MB/s) figure esp32.co.uk states for 4K ProRes 422 HQ (read 2026-11-08). Same scaling gives 4444 at 165 MB/s and 4444 XQ at 250 MB/s.

findings.label: Link ceilings in ProRes 422 HQ UHD 29.97 streams
findings.value: 2.5GbE 2 streams; 10GbE 11 streams; Thunderbolt 4 networking at 20 Gb/s 22 streams
findings.source_title: Best NAS for 4K Video Editing over 10GbE – Esp32.co.uk
findings.note: 312 MB/s ÷ 110 = 2.8 → 2; 1,250 ÷ 110 = 11.4 → 11; 2,500 ÷ 110 = 22.7 → 22. The 10GbE figure is already on the esp32 page; the 2.5GbE and TB4 ceilings are not. Whole streams only, no headroom for scrubbing.

findings.label: Measured Thunderbolt 4 read on a Mac (StorageReview, ATTO, M1 Max MacBook Pro, RAID 5 of five 3.84 TB SK hynix PE8110 E1.S)
findings.source_title: QNAP TBS-h574TX Thunderbolt 4 NAS Review - StorageReview.com
findings.note: Review dated April 2, 2024, by Vince Carnevale. Derived: 1,850 ÷ 110 = 16.8 → 16 ProRes 422 HQ UHD streams; 1,850 ÷ 165 = 11 ProRes 4444 streams.

findings.label: Measured Thunderbolt 4 read on Windows 11 (StorageReview, Blackmagic Disk Speed Test)
findings.source_title: QNAP TBS-h574TX Thunderbolt 4 NAS Review - StorageReview.com
findings.note: Derived: 1,015 ÷ 110 = 9.2 → 9 streams on Windows vs 16 on the Mac, from the same box and drives. 10GbE on Windows 10 measured 868 MB/s read → 868 ÷ 110 = 7.9 → 7 streams.

findings.label: Price per measured MB/s (enclosure only)
findings.source_title: QNAP TBS-h574TX Thunderbolt 4 NAS Review - StorageReview.com
findings.note: $1,449 MSRP (i5/16 GB, April 2024, per StorageReview) ÷ 1,850 MB/s = $0.78; ÷ 868 MB/s = $1.67. Drives not included; QNAP's US page shows no price.

findings.label: Measured 10GbE SMB read, RAID 5 of six Seagate IronWolf Pro 20 TB (ComputerBase, 5.9 GB file / 15 GB folder)
findings.value: 420.7 MB/s file read, 320.2 MB/s folder read; 486.4 MB/s file write
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP6800 Pro im Test: Übertragungsraten und Backup - ComputerBase
findings.note: Review dated June 6, 2024, by Frank Hüber, early UGOS firmware. Derived: 420.7 ÷ 110 = 3.8 → 3 ProRes 422 HQ UHD streams from the HDD pool; 320.2 ÷ 110 → 2 for a folder of clips. Roughly a third of the 11-stream link ceiling.

findings.label: Measured 10GbE SMB read, two-NVMe volume (Seagate IronWolf 510 480 GB), ComputerBase
findings.value: 761.5 MB/s file read, 636.3 MB/s file write
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP6800 Pro im Test: Übertragungsraten und Backup - ComputerBase
findings.note: Derived: 761.5 ÷ 110 = 6.9 → 6 streams from the NVMe volume vs 3 from HDDs. With 2× 10GbE bonded, the SSD volume read 1,055.9 MB/s → 9 streams; the HDD volume read 499 MB/s → 4 streams.

findings.label: Thunderbolt 4 direct-attach copy, 25 GB, HDD volume (ComputerBase, derived from stated times)
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP6800 Pro im Test: Übertragungsraten und Backup - ComputerBase
findings.note: ComputerBase states 0:59 read and 0:47 write for 25 GB over Thunderbolt 4: 25,000 MB ÷ 59 s = 424 MB/s; 25,000 ÷ 47 = 532 MB/s. Derived: 424 ÷ 110 = 3 streams, the same as 10GbE, because the HDD pool is the limit, not the link.

findings.note: Price via storecheck on 2026-11-08, in stock, diskless. $1,099.99 ÷ 420.7 MB/s = $2.61; ÷ 761.5 = $1.45.

unsourced: Apple's ProRes white paper 4K data-rate table: the PDF downloaded but text extraction was blocked, so the 110 MB/s UHD figure is derived from Apple's 1080p figure × 4 and cross-checked against esp32.co.uk, not read from the table.
Blackmagic RAW data rates per compression ratio: Blackmagic's product page carries them only as an image, so no BRAW stream counts.
Sony XAVC HS / S-I 4K bit rates for an H.265 or All-Intra stream count: Sony's help guide and US product page would not load.

UGREEN's own 600–700 MB/s RAID 5 claim for the DXP4800 Plus and the DXP6800 Pro's Thunderbolt and warranty text: nas.ugreen.com product pages returned HTTP 429 three times; prices came through the store tool.
A named Thunderbolt 4 measurement for the DXP480T Plus on a Mac: only a Reddit user post (900–1,000 MB/s write, up to 2,000 MB/s read) exists, so it is left out.
